summary.text: World War II was a global conflict, from 1 September 1939 to 2 September 1945, between the Allies and the Axis powers, with nearly all the world's countries taking part.
It was the deadliest conflict in history, causing the deaths of 60 to 75 million people, a majority of them civilians.
It left behind the United Nations, two rival superpowers, and the decolonisation of Africa and Asia as Europe's great powers lost influence.

facts.label: Deaths
facts.value: 60 to 75 million, a majority of them civilians

facts.label: How it began
facts.value: Nazi Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939

facts.label: Japan's surrender
facts.value: Announced on 15 August, signed on 2 September 1945

facts.label: United Nations
facts.value: Five victorious powers hold permanent Security Council seats

items.prompt: Nazi Germany invades Poland on 1 September 1939. How do Britain and France respond?

options.label: They sign a peace deal with Germany
They invade the Soviet Union
They declare war on Germany
They wait a year before acting

items.explain: After the invasion of Poland, the United Kingdom and France declared war on Germany.

items.prompt: Germany opens a new front in the east in June 1941. Whom is it attacking?

options.label: The Soviet Union
Japan
The United States
Italy

items.explain: In June 1941, Germany invaded the Soviet Union, opening the Eastern Front.

items.prompt: In December 1941 Japan attacks American and British territories in Asia and the Pacific, including Pearl Harbor. What follows?

options.label: The United States joins the Axis side
The United States enters the war against the Axis
Japan withdraws after its early gains
The United States stays out until 1945

items.explain: The attacks led the United States to enter the war against the Axis.

items.prompt: Which conditions are named among the causes of the war?

options.label: A shortage of food after World War I and a boom in trade
The United Nations and a rivalry between the superpowers
Decolonisation in Africa and a peace treaty with Japan
Unresolved tensions after World War I, fascism in Europe and militarism in Japan

items.explain: Causes included unresolved tensions after World War I and the rise of fascism in Europe and militarism in Japan.

items.prompt: Japan announced its surrender on 15 August 1945, yet a formal date is also given. Why is there more than one date for the war's end?

options.label: The armistice of 15 August was accepted at the time, but the formal surrender on 2 September officially ended the war in Asia
The war in Asia ended on 8 May, the same day Europe's war did, so both dates are wrong
Japan surrendered on 2 September and then surrendered again on 15 August
The war only ended when a peace treaty was signed in 1951

items.explain: The armistice was generally accepted at the time as the end, but the formal surrender on 2 September officially ended the war in Asia.

items.prompt: Europe's great powers are devastated and their influence wanes. What does that trigger?

options.label: A European empire that grew stronger overseas
The end of the United Nations
The decolonisation of Africa and Asia
A return to the balance of power of 1914

items.explain: In the wake of Europe's devastation, the waning influence of its great powers triggered the decolonisation of Africa and Asia.
